findings.claim: The rewritten condition only rejects `NaN`; all other invalid request-id values (undefined, booleans, objects, arrays, functions) now pass the assertion and are unsoundly typed as `number | string | null`.
findings.rationale: The new predicate is `obj !== null && typeof obj === 'number' && isNaN(obj) && typeof obj !== 'string'`. Because `typeof obj === 'number'` is required, the only value satisfying every conjunct is `NaN`. The previous predicate threw for anything that was not null / string / finite-or-infinite number. This is a clear validation regression on untrusted wire input parsed by the RPC message parser, and the `asserts obj is number | string | null` signature makes it a lie to all downstream callers. High confidence.

findings.claim: The `typeof obj !== 'string'` clause is unreachable/dead after `typeof obj === 'number'` in the same conjunction.
findings.rationale: Once `typeof obj === 'number'` has been asserted, `typeof obj !== 'string'` is always true, so the clause contributes nothing. It is a strong signal the refactor of the boolean expression was mechanical rather than semantics-preserving. High confidence this clause is redundant as written.
